newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwab Versand plans Russia distribution by air cargo.
newsitem.headline: Schwab Versand plans Russia distribution by air cargo.

text.p: German mail-order company Schwab Versand GmbH said it will need to use selected air cargo services for its forthcoming Russia expansion.

The firm, a subsidiary of Hamburg-based Otto Versand, said it will distribute brochures and catalogues in post offices across Russia under a new co-operation agreement between the Russian and German national post offices.

Export manager Robert Laembgen told Reuters that German goods ordered by fax and destined for remote regions and cities would have to be flown as part of a multi-modal distribution strategy for Russian deliveries.
In a St Petersburg pilot scheme, the company currently distributed by truck, rail or ship but nationwide expansion, in particular to Siberia, would require air transport services, he said.
Schwab was targeting the expanding Russian middle-class, amounting to 5-10 percent of the population and which had a reasonable standard of living, he added.
It was too early to assess demand in Russia for mail-order consumer goods, Laembgen said.

But small electrical goods and textiles costing less than 100 dollars and thus duty-free, under Russian customs regulations were likely to be the most popular products, he forecast. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
